cover.headline: A very profitable injectables core finally showing through, priced about where its post-Cenexi history says it should be
cover.lead: Gland Pharma makes generic and complex injectables for partners (US generic companies, big pharma, tender agencies) from four Indian sites, and since April 2023 owns Cenexi, a French-Belgian contract manufacturer. Of FY26 revenue of ₹6,431 cr, 71% was the base business (36.5% EBITDA margin) and 29% Cenexi (a small loss); 53% went to the US. Growth has returned: Q1FY27 revenue +20% (~15% in constant currency), EBITDA margin 27.2%, Cenexi in profit, and a 55-SKU contract-manufacturing deal from 2029. The stock rose ~75% in 2026 to ₹2,899 on 30-Sep-2026, even as Fosun sold 6% on 4-Sep. Brokers that disclose a method all use **P/E** (Motilal Oswal 30x 12-month forward, ICICI Direct 33x FY28E, Nomura 27.5x FY28-29E). We forecast EPS of ₹79.7 / ₹97.9 / ₹119.0 for FY27-29E. Gland's own one-year-forward P/E median since the Cenexi deal closed (25.4x), times the pharma peers' move over the same window (×1.092), gives **27.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹108.6 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD**. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,877, DCF ₹2,312. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: The base business earned a 36.5% EBITDA margin in FY26 and 40% in Q4FY26, on 1.7 bn units of sterile capacity, 342 approved ANDAs and a regulatory record without a warning letter or import alert. Its cost position wins US GPO contracts and big-pharma transfers from European plants that cost 5-6x more to run. Few Indian companies can match it in injectables.

arguments.h: Cenexi has been the drag, and is only now turning
arguments.p: Cenexi cost ~€230 mn (enterprise value), needs a ~€60 mn capex plan (2025-27) and lost money for three years (EBITDA −€19 mn in FY25). It made €2 mn in Q1FY27. We model a 5% / 8% / 10% margin for FY27-29E, below management's mid-teens goal, because every Cenexi target so far has slipped.

arguments.h: Growth is back, but the big drivers are back-ended
arguments.p: We forecast revenue +16.5% / +13.6% / +14.1%, a little below management's new ~20% four-year ambition. The 55-SKU deal starts in CY2029, GLP-1 US volumes in FY30-31 and the large complex injectables after FY29. Medium-term guidance moved from 'low-20s' (May-2025) to 15% (May-2026) to ~20% (Aug-2026).

arguments.h: The price already reflects the recovery
arguments.p: At ₹2,899 the stock trades at 36.4x our FY27E and 29.6x FY28E EPS. Our 27.5x is the post-acquisition median lifted 9.2% for a sector that trades above its history; the since-2021 median (30.0x, ×1.082) would justify ~₹3,530, but it mixes standalone-Gland prices and the 2021 bubble. Below ~₹2,600 the rule would make us buyers.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the Cenexi summer quarter, base-business margin after the Q1 currency help, and the updated four-year growth outlook management promised for "next quarter".
USFDA approval of the new ready-to-use bag line (management hoped for August-September 2026) and the ophthalmic/BFS lines; the Saudi NUPCO tender awards.
Deepak Sapra (ex-Dr. Reddy's) joins as CEO from 16-Nov-2026, filling a gap since April 2026.
Fosun: two 6% sales in two years and no disclosed lock-up; a further sale would add supply, though the last block was absorbed by domestic funds.
GLP-1 partner launches outside the US (e.g., a Canada filing that could launch in Q4FY27) and new CDMO contracts.

sections.title: One sterile-manufacturing platform sold three ways: own filings marketed by partners, partners' filings, and contract manufacturing (now including Cenexi)

blocks.p: Gland develops and makes injectable medicines (vials, lyophilised vials, ampoules, pre-filled syringes, bags, cartridges and ophthalmics) and sells almost nothing under its own name. Its customers are US generic companies (including Fosun's US arm), big-pharma companies outsourcing production, and tender agencies in emerging markets. It runs four Indian formulation sites (Dundigal and Pashamylaram in Hyderabad, a penem plant, and an oncology plant at Visakhapatnam), API plants, and Cenexi's four sites in France and Belgium, with 1.7 bn units of capacity and ~4,300 employees in India. It has filed 389 US ANDAs (342 approved) and holds 1,828 product registrations worldwide.

blocks.p: **Concentration is real but has eased.** One customer accounted for ₹870 cr (13.5%) of FY26 revenue; two customers for ₹1,389 cr (24.7%) in FY25 (AR FY26 note 43). Sales to Fosun Pharma USA, a related party, were ₹244 cr (3.8%). Because partners own the front end, Gland rarely knows end-market approvals in advance (management cannot forecast GLP-1 volumes for this reason) and can lose a product if a partner re-sources or fails, as Athenex's bankruptcy showed in FY23.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Gland is a manufacturing franchise, not a drug company. It wins on cost, breadth and compliance, and shares the upside of its own filings with partners. That makes margins high and capital needs modest, but it also leaves Gland a step removed from pricing and demand, and dependent on a few large partners and on Cenexi's turnaround for its European ambitions.

sections.title: Forty-eight years of sterile manufacturing, a Chinese parent since 2017, one customer shock and one expensive acquisition

blocks.p: Dr. P.V.N. Raju founded Gland in Hyderabad in 1978 as a contract maker of small-volume injectables. It built its business on partner-led US generics after the Dundigal plant won USFDA approval in 2003. Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical bought 74% in October 2017 (reported at ~US$1.09 bn) and listed Gland in November 2020 at ₹1,500 a share, India's largest pharma IPO at the time (₹6,480 cr, of which ₹1,250 cr new money). Fosun has since sold two 6% blocks (June 2024 and September 2026) and owns ~45.8%. The numbers fall into five eras.

blocks.callout: **Lesson from history:** Gland's two big setbacks came from outside the plants: a partner's failure and the loss of tender and partner volumes in FY23, and an acquisition that took three years longer than planned to break even. Its manufacturing and compliance have been consistently good. Investors should weigh partner, pricing and capital-allocation risks more heavily than operational ones.

sections.title: Industry: generic injectables grow faster than pills, contract manufacturing is moving east, and GLP-1 generics are a 2030 prize

blocks.p: **Generic injectables** are a harder business than tablets: sterile manufacturing is expensive, regulators inspect it closely, and the US suffers recurring shortages when plants fail. Gland's annual report cites a global generic injectables market of ~US$135.4 bn in 2025 growing ~11.5% a year to US$401.8 bn by 2035 (an industry estimate; we treat it as an upper bound), within a global medicines market IQVIA sees at ~US$2.4 tn by 2029. Prices still fall: Gland's US volumes rose 9% in FY25 while prices fell 5%, and management describes the US market as growing ~3-4% a year, with Gland gaining share through GPO contracts on a lower cost base.

**Contract manufacturing (CDMO)** is the growth engine. Big-pharma and specialty companies run sterile production in Europe and the US at costs management puts at 5-6x India's, across 80-100 sites; they want fewer, cheaper partners with clean records. The biologics CDMO market alone is put at US$17.1 bn (2024) rising to US$38.1 bn by 2030. **GLP-1 generics** (liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide) open market by market from 2026, but the US, the biggest prize, comes around 2031-32; pen and cartridge fill-finish capacity is scarce, which is why Gland built 140 mn units of it.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the tailwinds visible in today's numbers are US share gains and the weak rupee; the ones the stock is excited about (GLP-1, big-pharma transfers, complex injectables) are real and contracted but arrive mostly after FY29. Our forecasts give them little credit before then, which is the main reason we sit below management's ~20% growth ambition.

sections.title: Base business: US launches and GPO wins took growth from −1% to +24% in a year, at 36-40% margins; rest of world and India lag

blocks.p: The base business (Gland ex-Cenexi) is where the money is made. Revenue was ₹4,177 cr in FY24, ₹4,125 cr in FY25 and ₹4,561 cr in FY26 (+11%), with EBITDA margins of 34%, 35% and 36.5%. In Q1FY27 it grew ~24% (19-20% in constant currency, CFO), led by the US (+32%): Dalbavancin (launched February 2026; the partner won a Vizient contract), the multivitamin infusion (April 2026; competitive generic therapy exclusivity, "a very difficult product to make") and Sugammadex (approved and launched 29-Jul-2026), plus volume gains in enoxaparin, vancomycin, chlorothiazide and heparin. Gland launched 31 products in the US in FY26 and four in Q1FY27.

blocks.p: **Rest of world** (₹1,112 cr in FY26, 17%) is the weak spot: Saudi Arabia's NUPCO moved enoxaparin to a local partner in FY25, shipments stopped during the West Asia conflict in Q4FY26, and Q1FY27 revenue was flat (+2%) while tender awards were delayed. Management once said this business could double in 3-5 years (May-2025); it has not grown since. **Canada, Australia and New Zealand** fell 28% in Q1FY27 on lower volumes. **India** (₹267 cr in FY26, 4%) is small; the B2C branded business shrank 23% in FY26. **Europe** for the base business is mostly licensing and Gland products released through Cenexi (₹188 cr in FY26).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the base business is a high-quality generic-injectables franchise whose growth depends on a steady flow of launches to offset ~5% annual price erosion. FY27's +24% start owes much to three launches and the rupee; we model +18% for FY27, +15% and +16% after, at a 36-37% margin (management guides 33-35%).

sections.title: Cenexi: three years after the deal, a €200 mn business at breakeven; the turnaround is real but slower than every target set for it

blocks.p: Gland agreed to buy Cenexi in November 2022 and completed on 27-Apr-2023, paying up to €120 mn for the equity (enterprise value €230 mn). The stated logic: a foothold in European contract manufacturing, technologies Gland lacked (hormones, controlled substances, vaccines, oral solids), Cenexi's customers, and a European release site for Gland's own products. The four sites (Fontenay and Osny near Paris, Hérouville in Normandy, Braine-l'Alleud in Belgium) carry high European labour costs. Cenexi lost money from the start: EBITDA of −€9 mn in its first eleven months (FY24) and −€19 mn in FY25, while management promised breakeven by December 2025 and a double-digit margin in FY27. In FY26 revenue rose 11% to €182 mn and EBITDA improved by €16 mn to −€3 mn (−1.8%), with three profitable quarters; Q1FY27 brought €48 mn of revenue and €2 mn of EBITDA (4%).

blocks.p: **What is changing.** Contract renegotiations to pass on inflation, workforce cuts, two products launched at Hérouville in 2025 (an inactivated vaccine and a sterile ophthalmic gel), new ampoule capacity at Fontenay (one line ramping, a second high-capacity line from early 2027 adding ~30 mn ampoules), a vial/lyo block at Braine by end-2027, and new hormonal and orphan-drug syringe contracts. Gland also now uses Cenexi as the European arm of group deals: the 55-SKU agreement signed in August 2026 needed Cenexi for EU packaging and release ("without Cenexi, this wouldn't have happened").

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Cenexi has stopped losing money, which removes a drag of ~₹176 cr of EBITDA (FY25) from the group. But on the capital invested (€230 mn of enterprise value, a ~€60 mn capex plan for 2025-27 and three years of losses) it still earns almost nothing; an investor on the May-2025 call called it poor capital allocation, and the CFO conceded it was "taking longer than what we estimated". We model 5% / 8% / 10% EBITDA margins and revenue +13% / +10% / +9% in rupees; the mid-teens margin management targets is our bull case.

sections.title: CDMO and pipeline: contracts signed in 2026 are large, but their revenue mostly lands in FY29-31

blocks.p: Contract manufacturing (CDMO, called tech transfer in the annual report) was ₹2,940 cr in FY26 (46% of revenue, +29%), of which Cenexi ₹1,869 cr and Gland's own CDMO work ~₹1,071 cr (+33%). In Q1FY27 CDMO revenue grew 20% to ₹892 cr, half of the total. Management expects CDMO and B2B to stay ~50:50 for two years and CDMO to become the larger after CY2029. Gland is honest that this is mostly generic and specialty manufacturing: "we don't have any innovative products right now" (Srinivas Sadu, 10-Aug-2026); innovator work under discussion is on peptides.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the 2026 contract wins are the best evidence yet that big pharma will move sterile production to Gland, and they validate the Cenexi purchase as a door-opener. But the timing is long: the big contract, GLP-1 and the large complex products all fall in FY29-31, beyond the earnings the market will look at in twelve months. sections.title: Capacity and compliance: plants near full, a ~₹2,000 cr expansion, and a clean USFDA record

blocks.p: Gland's Indian plants run at ~80-90% utilisation, with bag and ophthalmic lines the tightest; Fontenay is ~100% and Osny ~90%, while Hérouville and Braine have room (50-60%). Capex was ₹398 cr (FY24), ₹394 cr (FY25) and ₹494 cr (FY26, 7.7% of sales), low for a manufacturer because Gland built ahead in FY20-22. In May 2026 it announced a ~₹2,000 cr programme over 3-5 years (vial, BFS, ophthalmic and liposome lines at Pashamylaram Suite 10, a ₹165 cr oncology isolator line for the new CDMO contract, a sterile-API block, and Cenexi lines). FY27 capex is guided at ~₹550 cr. Revenue per rupee of gross block fell from 2.1x (FY22) to 0.9x (FY26), mostly because Cenexi's land, buildings and plants came onto the books in FY24.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a real cost-and-compliance moat in sterile manufacturing; no pricing power, and partners own the customer

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Gland's is the hardest kind to build in generics: low-cost, high-quality sterile manufacturing at scale, across almost every injectable format, with a clean regulatory record. It shows in 35-40% base-business margins against ~20% for most generic peers and in big pharma choosing Gland for transfers. It does not show in pricing, which keeps falling, or in control of the end customer, which sits with partners.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** a genuine but narrow moat. Sterile capacity, compliance and cost are hard to copy and are why Gland wins share; but Aurobindo's Eugia, Caplin Steriles and many US and Chinese makers compete in the same molecules, and partners can re-source a product after a re-filing. Cenexi adds European access but no cost advantage. The group returns (ROE ~10%) are below its cost of equity today, so the moat has yet to show up for shareholders.

sections.title: Quarters: Cenexi makes Q2 the weak quarter (European summer shutdown); launches and GPO wins lifted the last three

blocks.p: Gland's quarters move with partner orders, launches and tender timing rather than a season, with one exception: Cenexi shuts its French and Belgian plants for maintenance every summer, so the September quarter is weak (Cenexi lost €6 mn of EBITDA in Q2FY26 and €8 mn in Q2FY25). The base business lifted revenue from ₹1,041 cr in Q1FY26 to ₹1,265 cr in Q4FY26 as Dalbavancin, the multivitamin infusion and new GPO contracts arrived; Q4FY26's 29% consolidated margin included a 40% base-business margin with milestone income of ~6% of revenue. Q1FY27: revenue ₹1,800 cr (+20%; ~15% in constant currency), EBITDA margin 27.2%, PAT ₹317 cr.

sections.title: Four acts: a fast-growing standalone to FY22, a collapse in FY23, a costly European acquisition, and a recovery that only in FY27 takes EPS past the FY22 peak

blocks.p: Gland grew revenue from ₹994 cr in FY15 to ₹4,401 cr in FY22 at 34-42% EBITDA margins, selling injectables through US partners; Covid-era demand lifted FY21-22. FY23 broke the run: a partner (Athenex) went bankrupt, another customer was lost, Chinese rivals undercut enoxaparin and heparin, and revenue fell 18% to ₹3,625 cr. The Cenexi acquisition (April 2023) then added ~₹1,500 cr of revenue at a loss, so FY24 revenue jumped 56% while the margin fell to 24% and EPS stayed at ~₹47. FY25 was the low point (revenue −1%, EPS ₹42.4). FY26 recovered: revenue +14.5% to ₹6,431 cr, margin 25.3%, EPS ₹62.35, and Q1FY27 EPS of ₹19.2 puts the twelve months to June 2026 at ₹68.5. Six years after FY20 (EPS ₹49.9), per-share earnings have grown only ~4% a year.

blocks.p: Before Cenexi, Gland's EBITDA margin ran at 34-42% (FY17-22) and fell to 28% in FY23 with the customer losses. Cenexi changed the shape of the P&L: it has a ~76-80% gross margin (contract manufacturing uses customers' materials) but very high European labour costs, so group employee costs jumped from 11% of sales (FY23) to 22-25% (FY24-26) and the EBITDA margin fell to 23-24%. FY26 recovered to 25.3% (base 36.5%, Cenexi −1.8%) and Q1FY27 to 27.2% (base ~36.6%, Cenexi 4%). Gross margin (revenue less materials) has risen from 53.5% (FY23) to 65.1% (FY26) on Cenexi, mix, yields and procurement.

sections.title: Net cash of ₹3,100-3,300 cr (a third of equity), but working capital ties up ~38% of sales and depresses returns

blocks.p: Gland holds ₹3,359 cr of cash and deposits (Mar-2026; ₹3,547 cr at Jun-2026) against ₹243 cr of debt at Cenexi and ₹40 cr of leases: net cash ₹3,116 cr on the company's basis, ₹3,294 cr at June. About a third of shareholders' equity sits in cash earning ~6.5%, which is one reason ROE is only ~10%. The business is working-capital heavy for a B2B manufacturer: inventory is ~284 days of material cost and receivables ~107 days (Screener, FY26); the company's own cash-conversion cycle improved from 172 days (FY25) to 164 (FY26) and 155 (Jun-2026). Inventory write-downs were ₹156 cr in FY26 (₹121 cr in FY25). Cash generation is steady: operating cash flow of ₹915-1,031 cr a year in FY25-26, capex of ~₹400-500 cr, the first dividends (₹329 cr paid in FY25, ₹297 cr in FY26) and the ₹1,022 cr Cenexi purchase in FY24.

blocks.p: Gland has made one acquisition (Cenexi: ₹1,022 cr paid in FY24, plus ₹777 cr of Cenexi debt repaid and a ~€60 mn Cenexi capex plan for 2025-27) and started paying dividends in FY25 (₹18 and ₹20 a share; ~₹300-330 cr a year; yield ~0.7% at ₹2,899). The result: ROE fell from ~21-24% (FY20-21) to 7.8% (FY25) and 10.5% (FY26), below our 11.9% cost of equity; return on operating capital (excluding cash) recovered to ~17%. blocks.p: Fosun Pharma Industrial Pte (Singapore), a subsidiary of Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical, owned 51.83% at March 2026 (51.77% of the larger June-2026 share count). blocks.p: House rule (PLAYBOOK §4, §7c): the stock's own one-year-forward P/E median, leaving out trough years, times the pharma sector factor, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Gland's window starts at the Cenexi completion (27-Apr-2023) so that the multiple's history and our forecast EPS are both on Gland-plus-Cenexi earnings; a window shorter than five years pairs with the peers' move over the same window. No blend with Gland's own re-rating and no growth uplift; those are sensitivities below.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than its last five years suggest, at a price that already knows it

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest pure-play injectables manufacturer: a base business earning 36-40% EBITDA margins on low-cost, compliant sterile capacity across every format; a European CDMO (Cenexi) that has just stopped losing money; signed contracts with big pharma, GLP-1 developers and a Chinese liposome developer that start to pay from FY28-30; and ₹3,300 cr of net cash. Earnings should grow ~24% a year to FY29E on our numbers, from a depressed base.

**What you are paying:** 36.4x our FY27E and 29.6x FY28E EPS after a ~75% rise in 2026. Our 27.5x Sep-28E multiple is Gland's own median since the Cenexi deal (25.4x) lifted 9.2% for a sector trading above its history; it gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The DCF (₹2,312) is lower. The since-2021 median (30.0x) would support more, but it prices a standalone Gland in the 2021 boom, before Cenexi and before FY23's shock.

blocks.p: **Why HOLD and not BUY, given the momentum?** Because the rule compares the price with a target built from the multiple the market has paid for this Gland (with Cenexi) since 2023, and the price is already there. The drivers that would justify more (the 55-SKU contract, GLP-1 in the US, large complex launches) arrive after the twelve months the target covers, and management's growth guidance has moved twice in a year. A strong Q2, the bag-line approval or an early GLP-1 launch could carry the stock higher for a while; we would raise estimates on delivered numbers, not on ambitions.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Gland Pharma (consolidated, Rs crore). Gland reports one segment (pharmaceuticals); until FY26 it split the P&L into the base business (Gland ex-Cenexi) and Cenexi (France/Belgium CDMO, acquired 27-Apr-2023), and from Q1FY27 into CDMO vs B2B. The engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and EBITDA margin; the two-line build (base business and Cenexi, revenue and EBITDA) sits in businessLines and tools/authoring/GLAND.ctx.js checks it equals model revenue and EBITDA. Other income = treasury yield x opening net cash (engine treasury) + interest on the cash held against Cenexi's debt and leases + small recurring items; no forex gains are forecast. Valued on P/E, as the brokers that disclose a method do.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two-line build (businessLines). FY27E +16.5%: Q1FY27 revenue Rs1,800 cr (+19.6%; constant currency ~15%, CFO 10-Aug-2026); management guides at least 15% constant-currency growth for FY27, with upside if the bag line is approved by the USFDA in Q3 (Srinivas Sadu, 10-Aug-2026); the weaker rupee adds a few points in H1. FY28E +13.6%: management's step 'FY28 could be 15%' (15-May-2026), from CDMO contracts (the NDDS oncology CDMO from H2FY28, USD25-30 mn a year), settlement launches, co-developed products and Cenexi's new Fontenay ampoule line (early 2027); we stay a little below because Gland's medium-term guidance has been cut and raised within a year (May-2025: low-20s for FY27-28; May-2026: 12-13% for FY27 and 15% CAGR; Aug-2026: ~20% CAGR). FY29E +14.1%: complex launches in Q2-Q3FY29 (management's 'one big step up'); the 55-SKU strategic CDMO agreement (USD90-100 mn at peak) only starts in CY2029, so it adds almost nothing to FY29. GLP-1 fill-finish is excluded by management from guidance (major US volumes FY30-31) and by us. Street: ICICI Direct FY27E Rs7,537 cr / FY28E Rs8,769 cr (11-Aug-2026); Elara FY27E Rs7,502 cr, FY28E Rs8,585 cr, FY29E Rs9,436 cr (16-May-2026, before Q1).

base._why: FY26 consolidated revenue Rs64,307 mn = base business Rs45,613 mn + Cenexi Rs18,693 mn (EUR182 mn) (Q4FY26 investor presentation, 15-May-2026).

businessLines._why: Base business (Gland ex-Cenexi): FY26 Rs4,561 cr (+10.6%), Q1FY27 +24% (19-20% constant currency, CFO 10-Aug-2026) on US +32% (Dalbavancin, multivitamin infusion with CGT exclusivity, Sugammadex launched 29-Jul-2026, GPO contract wins). Quarterly growth fades through FY27 as Dalbavancin (launched Feb-2026) and the Q3-Q4FY26 GPO wins enter the base: +18% for the year. +15% in FY28 and +16% in FY29 (CDMO ramp-ups, RTU bags, complex launches from Q2FY29). Reported EBITDA margin (after ESOP cost): 35.0% (FY25), 36.5% (FY26), 36.6% in Q1FY27 (GAM: Rs4,930 mn less Cenexi's EUR2 mn); management guides 33-35% for the base (15-May-2026); 36.0% / 36.5% / 37.0% as utilisation rises and CDMO mix grows, partly offset by US price erosion and higher ESOP cost under the 2025 scheme. Cenexi: EUR164 mn (FY25), EUR182 mn (FY26), EUR48 mn in Q1FY27; guidance 'near EUR200 million and high single-digit margins' for FY27 (Neha M., confirmed by management, 10-Aug-2026); Q2 is the summer-shutdown quarter (Q2FY26 EBITDA -EUR6 mn). Rupee value +13% in FY27E (EUR~198 mn at ~Rs107), +10% in FY28E (new Fontenay ampoule line adds ~30 mn ampoules from early 2027) and +9% in FY29E. EBITDA margin -11.8% (FY25), -1.8% (FY26), 4% in Q1FY27: 5% / 8% / 10% vs management's 'mid-teen EBITDA in the midterm', because Cenexi's targets have slipped every year (May-2025: breakeven by Dec-2025 and double-digit in FY27).

assumptions._marginWhy: Weighted from the two-line build: FY27E 27.3% (Q1FY27 27.2% on Screener's basis, which includes ESOP cost and a Rs3.6 cr forex loss), FY28E 28.7%, FY29E 30.0%. Consolidated EBITDA margin: 28.3% (FY23, pre-Cenexi), 23.5% (FY24), 22.6% (FY25), 25.3% (FY26). Management targets ~30% adjusted EBITDA (before ESOP) in the near term and 35% in 3-4 years (10-Aug-2026). Street FY27E: ICICI Direct 26.6%, Elara 26.3% (pre-Q1).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs494 cr (Screener cash flow; company Rs4,938 mn); Q1FY27 Rs113 cr. Management: 'this year, we are going to spend about INR 550 crores capex. And this will scale up as and when we start building the brownfield' (Srinivas Sadu, 10-Aug-2026), including a Rs165 cr oncology isolator line for the new CDMO contract and a sterile-API block for the Neuland collaboration; the ~Rs2,000 cr programme runs over 3-5 years (vial, ophthalmic, BFS, liposome lines at Pashamylaram Suite 10; Cenexi BLA vial/lyo block and Fontenay ampoule line). Rs700 cr in FY28E and Rs750 cr in FY29E.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs424 cr = 6.8% of average gross block (Rs6,199 cr, Screener; gross block includes Rs1,118 cr of land); Q1FY27 Rs111 cr (Rs445 cr annualised) = ~6.4% of gross block. The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP held flat), so 6.4% gives ~Rs452 / 492 / 538 cr in FY27-29E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash net of borrowings (engine treasury: Rs3,359 cr of cash and deposits less Rs284 cr of borrowings and leases at Mar-26 = Rs3,075 cr). Interest on term deposits was Rs203 cr in FY25 and Rs205 cr in FY26 (AR FY26 note 25), 6.5% of average gross cash (Rs2,952 cr at Mar-25 incl. Rs396 cr of non-callable deposits; Rs3,359 cr at Mar-26). Q1FY27 other income Rs61 cr, 'primarily interest income' (CFO), ~7.1% annualised on average cash including small items. Deposit rates are lower after the 2025 repo-rate cuts: 6.25% in FY27E, 6.0% after.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Two sourced parts. (1) Interest on the gross cash that the engine nets against borrowings: Rs284 cr (Cenexi's external debt and leases) x the same treasury yield = Rs18 cr in FY27E and Rs17 cr after; the matching interest cost sits in the interest line. (2) Recurring items: miscellaneous income Rs14.8 cr (FY26), Rs7.8 cr (FY25), plus small gains on investments and write-backs: Rs15 cr a year. Net forex gains (Rs92 cr in FY26, of which Rs51 cr in Q4; a Rs3.6 cr loss in Q1FY27, booked in other expenses) are not forecast. FY27E other income = Rs192 + 18 + 15 = ~Rs225 cr vs Rs224 cr ex-forex in FY26 (Rs316 cr reported less Rs92 cr forex) and ~Rs232 cr ex-forex in the twelve months to Jun-26.
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs33 cr in FY26 (incl. Rs2.1 cr of lease interest), Rs4.4 cr in Q1FY27 (Rs18 cr annualised). Cenexi's external debt was Rs243 cr at Mar-26 (CFO, 15-May-2026); we hold it flat (its interest is matched by the interest-income gross-up in otherIncome).
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective rate 34.3% (FY25), 29.4% (FY26; company), 27.1% in Q1FY27; Cenexi's losses earn no tax credit, so the blended rate falls as Cenexi turns profitable (CFO, 15-May-2026). Indian rate ~25.2%. 27% / 26% / 25.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend of Rs18 a share for FY25 (42% of EPS) and Rs20 for FY26 (32%; record date Aug-2026). 27% / 25% / 24% of EPS keeps the dividend at ~Rs21-29 a share.

dcf._betaWhy: Net-cash B2B injectables maker with long partner contracts, but a volatile history (revenue -18% in FY23, -1% in FY25) and a controlling foreign parent: 0.9 gives a cost of equity of 11.9% (no net debt, so WACC = cost of equity).
dcf._tgWhy: Middle of the house 5-6% range: generic injectables grow with volumes but face US price erosion; CDMO outsourcing and India's cost advantage add to it.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from 14% (FY29E) to 8% by year 15: Gland grew revenue ~12% a year over FY20-26 including the Cenexi acquisition, ~10% organically.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 30%, about FY29E's level: the mix shift to CDMO and Cenexi's recovery offset continued generic price erosion; no move to management's 35% target in the DCF.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from 7-8% of sales (FY27-29E) to 6% by year 15: maintenance at about depreciation (~5.5% of sales) plus modest growth capex in an asset-light B2B model.
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital is ~38% of sales (inventory ~284 days of material cost, receivables ~107 days on Screener): every rupee of extra sales ties up ~38 paise.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Management's ~20% revenue CAGR plays out: the bag and ophthalmic lines are approved on time, GLP-1 partners launch outside the US early, the strategic CDMO contracts ramp ahead of plan and Cenexi reaches its mid-teen margin.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the brokers that disclose a method value Gland: P/E on forward EPS (Motilal Oswal 30x 12-month forward, ICICI Direct 33x FY28E, Nomura 27.5x FY28-29E average, Equirus 30x Sep-27E; Elara P/E on core EPS plus cash). 27.5x = Gland's own one-year-forward P/E median since the Cenexi acquisition closed (27-Apr-2023) of 25.4x (house forwardMedian from that date; no trough years, exceptional items immaterial) x 1.092, the nine pharma peers' move against their own medians over the same window (PLAYBOOK 7c: a window shorter than five years pairs with the peers' move over that window) = 27.7x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. The window starts at the acquisition so that the multiple's history and the forecast EPS are both on Gland-plus-Cenexi earnings. Sensitivities only: since-2021 median 30.0x x the five-year factor 1.082 = 32.5x (mixes pre-acquisition prices and the FY22 Covid-era dates at ~75x), all weekly closes, window from Apr-2024, own re-rating, street. Bull 33.0x (75th percentile 30.0x x 1.092); bear 25.0x (25th percentile 22.7x x 1.092).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check on the same basis: Gland's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since 27-Apr-2023 (EV at the weekly close with net cash at the latest March published / next full-year EBITDA, computed in tools/authoring/GLAND.ctx.js) of 15.0x x 1.051 (the nine peers' EV/EBITDA move over the same window) = 15.8x, rounded to 16.0x Sep-28E EBITDA, plus Sep-28E net cash. Bull 19.0x / bear 14.0x (75th / 25th percentiles x 1.051).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.9% cost of equity (net cash), terminal growth 5.5%, operating working capital ~38% of sales.
